aloe_vera.short_description: A succulent with thick, gel-filled leaves used traditionally for skin and digestive support.
aloe_vera.key_identifiers: Fleshy lance-shaped leaves in a basal rosette; serrated margins with soft teeth; grey-green surface.
preparation: Topical: fresh inner gel or gel-based creams
aloe_vera.growing_areas: Tropical and subtropical regions worldwide; commonly cultivated in pots.
aloe_vera.cautions: Latex (yellow sap) is a strong laxative—avoid during pregnancy and in children; may interact with some medicines.

curry_leaves.short_description: Aromatic leaves widely used in South Asian cuisine; valued for antioxidant and digestive benefits.
curry_leaves.key_identifiers: Pinnate leaves with 11–21 glossy leaflets; strong characteristic aroma when crushed.
curry_leaves.growing_areas: Native to India and Sri Lanka; cultivated across South and Southeast Asia and in warm climates.
curry_leaves.cautions: Generally considered safe as food; therapeutic use should be guided by a professional.

hibiscus.short_description: Ornamental shrub; leaves and flowers used traditionally for hair care and as a mild anti-inflammatory.
hibiscus.key_identifiers: Shiny serrated leaves; large showy flowers (red/pink/other colors) with prominent staminal column.
medicinal_uses: Tea from flowers (varies by species; H. sabdariffa commonly used)
preparation: Leaf/flower paste for hair oil or masks
hibiscus.growing_areas: Tropical and subtropical regions; common garden plant.
hibiscus.cautions: Effects vary by species; check species before internal use and consult a professional if pregnant or on medication.

neem.short_description: Evergreen tree famed in Ayurveda for antimicrobial, antiparasitic, and skin benefits.
neem.key_identifiers: Compound leaves with many serrated leaflets; bitter taste; clusters of small white flowers.
medicinal_uses: Topical for acne and minor skin infections
preparation: Mouth rinses or toothpastes containing neem extracts
neem.growing_areas: Indian subcontinent; now cultivated in many arid/tropical regions.
neem.cautions: Avoid high-dose internal use, especially in children and pregnancy; possible liver toxicity from concentrated extracts.
